rationale: The source bundles four independent obligations with different activation, phase and evidence: (1) GREEN: while the acceptance is RED, write the smallest legal implementation; (2) REFACTOR: only after the first pass, hold behavior fixed and respond to the seven metrics sensors; (3) false-GREEN guard: when dead-code-reachability flags newly implemented behavior, wire it through the real owner; (4) review-ready: before declaring completion, rerun the proof and clear every strict finding across all active profiles. requires/follows edges link the parts so that no part can be satisfied while another is skipped (GREEN is not completion, and review-ready needs every strict finding cleared). The generic loop shape (RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR -> full-profile proof; the phase changes the response, not the validator) is a shared policy node. Round 2: replaced the unknown activation fact governed_task with the known facts task_has_acceptance and task_term. Governed-loop membership is now recorded in the phase observer note.

parts.title: GREEN: smallest legal implementation of the failing acceptance

facts.note: Gate: governed coding work is driven by a behavioral acceptance.
Gate: the task is enrolled in the governed ATDD loop, its current behavioral acceptance is still RED, and implementation work is under way.
Hint only. Task wording that places the work inside the governed ATDD loop.
Context only, not a gate. The rule applies before any finding exists.

fires: The agent writes implementation code to make a failing behavioral acceptance pass.
A metrics sensor or construction-constraint finding appears while the acceptance is still RED.
doesNotFire: Work with no behavioral acceptance under the governed ATDD loop.
The acceptance has already passed. The REFACTOR and review-ready parts apply instead.

parts.given: a governed ATDD Bun task whose current behavioral acceptance is still RED
parts.when: you write implementation code to make that acceptance pass
parts.then: Write the smallest correct implementation that makes the current failing behavioral acceptance pass while respecting every active construction constraint.
prefer: Start from one failing behavioral acceptance. Keep the search on the missing behavior, and prefer a naturally simple implementation.
Reuse the nearest existing compliant contracts, components, dependencies and patterns. Implement the smallest path that makes the required behavior pass.
Add a new boundary or abstraction only when the current behavior actually needs it, that is, when no existing compliant path can express it.
Derive traceability metadata from the plan and the acceptance. Do not invent it.

Treat the rules from atdd_topology, bun_green_traceability_detector, bun_clean_architecture_detector, bun_fullstack_detector, bun_design_system_detector and bun_responsive_detector as limits on a legal GREEN. These cover traceability/topology, architecture/dependency direction, runtime, design-system and responsive. Other active profiles, especially tester, traceability and security, are equally binding.
`green-*` rules are a traceability family (implementation identity, proof, runtime, purpose, side, layer), not a phase. Leave them where they are. They constrain GREEN.
The seven metrics sensors may run at any time, even while the acceptance is RED, and they stay strict. Only your response changes with the phase.
Stop expanding scope once the acceptance passes and the construction constraints are satisfied.
avoid: Knowingly violating a construction constraint and planning to repair it later.
While RED: broadening the implementation just to optimize a quality metric, or gaming any finding.
While behavior is still being discovered: redesigning adjacent systems, generalizing for hypothetical callers, or doing unrelated cleanup.
Writing deliberately poor code. GREEN does not permit it.
Treating behavioral GREEN as the end of the coding loop.
unless: A narrow structural change may come before behavioral GREEN when the existing design makes the required behavior impossible to implement correctly. Preserve already-proven behavior and change only the verified blocker.
parts.why: GREEN and REFACTOR are different search problems, and splitting them does not change enforcement. GREEN finds the smallest legal implementation of the required behavior. Construction constraints define what counts as legal while behavior is being discovered.
evidence: The acceptance was RED when GREEN started and now passes against the implementation (behavioral GREEN).
The GREEN change introduces no construction-constraint finding and no finding from another active profile.
The change reuses existing compliant paths. Any new boundary or abstraction is justified because no existing compliant path could express the behavior.
verifier_detail: Term behavioral_green: the point where the current RED behavioral acceptance passes against the implementation. It proves the requested behavior exists. It is not yet the end of the coding loop.

Term construction_constraint: a rule that constrains what counts as a legal implementation while behavior is being discovered. This covers traceability and topology, architecture and dependency direction, runtime, design-system and responsive boundaries, plus every other active non-refactor profile such as security. In the coder profile these are the rules emitted by atdd_topology, bun_green_traceability_detector, bun_clean_architecture_detector, bun_fullstack_detector, bun_design_system_detector and bun_responsive_detector.
No dedicated detector (implementation type none). Compliance is judged from phase ordering, acceptance runs and profile results.

parts.title: REFACTOR only after GREEN, guided by the metrics sensors

facts.note: Gate: governed coding work is driven by a behavioral acceptance.
Gate: the task is enrolled in the governed ATDD loop, and its current behavioral acceptance has passed for the first time.
Context only. The part also applies with no open finding.
Judging whether a change adds behavior or games a metric needs judgement.

fires: The acceptance has just passed and the agent is improving the design.
A metrics sensor reports a finding after behavioral GREEN.
doesNotFire: The acceptance is still RED. The GREEN part applies instead.
Work with no behavioral acceptance under the governed ATDD loop.

parts.given: a governed ATDD Bun task whose current behavioral acceptance has passed for the first time (behavioral GREEN)
parts.when: you change code to improve its design, including in response to a metrics sensor finding
parts.then: Start REFACTOR only after behavioral GREEN. Keep the now-green behavior fixed, and address refactor-sensor findings one at a time by following each finding's Diagnose / Prefer / Avoid / Verify guidance.
prefer: The refactor sensors are the bun_ts_metrics_detector rules: coder.bun.complexity-cyclomatic, coder.bun.complexity-length, coder.bun.complexity-nesting, coder.bun.dead-code-reachability, coder.bun.duplication-intra-layer, coder.bun.quality-comments, coder.bun.quality-mi.
Address one finding at a time, using that finding's smell-specific Diagnose / Prefer / Avoid / Verify guidance.
Treat each finding as evidence of a design smell, not as the design objective. Fix the smell, not the number.
These sensors may run at any time and stay strict. The phase changes your response, not the validator.
avoid: Starting REFACTOR before the acceptance has passed for the first time.
Forcing a sensor violation just to keep a ceremonial phase boundary.
unless: If a refactor sensor is already satisfied by the smallest correct implementation, keep that result.
parts.why: GREEN and REFACTOR are different search problems, and splitting them does not change enforcement. REFACTOR uses the seven metrics findings as guided design sensors while preserving the behavior GREEN established.
evidence: REFACTOR changes happen after the acceptance first passed. The acceptance still passes, and no new behavior was added.
Each addressed sensor finding is cleared by a design change, not by gaming the metric.
verifier_detail: Term refactor_sensor: a quality finding whose metric is evidence of a design smell rather than the design objective itself. In the Bun coder profile these are the seven bun_ts_metrics_detector rules: complexity-cyclomatic, complexity-length, complexity-nesting, dead-code-reachability, duplication-intra-layer, quality-comments, quality-mi.
Sensors may run at any time and remain strict. The phase distinction changes the agent's response, not the validator.

parts.title: Wire new behavior through its real owner (no false GREEN)

facts.note: Gate: governed coding work is driven by a behavioral acceptance.

values: finding applies to newly implemented behavior
facts.note: Gate: the finding hits code added for the current behavior.
Context: the task is in the governed ATDD loop. Any phase after implementation started.

fires: A unit-level acceptance passes, but dead-code-reachability reports that the newly implemented code is unreachable from a production root.
doesNotFire: Dead-code findings on pre-existing code that the current behavior did not add. The REFACTOR part handles those.

parts.given: a governed ATDD Bun task where the acceptance for newly implemented behavior passes
parts.when: coder.bun.dead-code-reachability reports a finding on the newly implemented behavior
parts.then: Wire the new behavior through its real production owner before you treat it as complete.
avoid: Manufacturing an import edge to fake reachability.
parts.why: dead-code-reachability is the one sensor that can expose a false GREEN: a unit-level acceptance can pass against code that no production root can reach.
evidence: The new behavior is reachable from a production root through its real owner. No dead-code-reachability finding remains on it, and no artificial import edge was added.
verifier_detail: Among the seven refactor sensors, only dead-code-reachability can expose a false GREEN: a unit-level acceptance passing against code that no production root reaches.

parts.title: Review-ready only after full-profile proof

facts.note: Gate: governed coding work is driven by a behavioral acceptance.
Gate: the task is enrolled in the governed ATDD loop and the agent is about to declare it complete or review-ready. No new code change is required.
Needed to know which profiles (coder, tester, traceability, security, ...) must be green.

fires: The agent is about to declare a governed task complete or review-ready, even if there is no new code change.
doesNotFire: Work with no behavioral acceptance under the governed ATDD loop.

parts.given: a governed ATDD Bun task after behavioral GREEN and REFACTOR
parts.when: you are about to declare the task complete or review-ready
parts.then: Before you declare review-ready, rerun the behavioral proof, run the applicable ATDD Bun profiles, and correct every strict finding caused or exposed by the work.
prefer: Review-ready means the target behavior still passes and every active ATDD Bun profile is green, with every strict finding cleared. Only this state counts as completion.
Follow the loop: RED -> smallest legal behavioral GREEN -> guided REFACTOR -> full-profile proof.
avoid: Using phase ordering to suppress a validator, weaken a threshold, or leave a security, architecture, runtime, traceability or other active constraint violated. Phase ordering never waives strict enforcement. Review-ready work MUST pass all active profiles.
Declaring completion at behavioral GREEN. It only proves the behavior exists.
parts.why: Phase ordering never waives strict enforcement. GREEN and REFACTOR change the agent's response, not the validators, so completion requires the full-profile proof.
evidence: The behavioral proof was rerun before review and still passes.
The applicable ATDD Bun profiles were run and are all green. Every strict finding caused or exposed by the work is cleared.
verifier_detail: Term review_ready: the point after behavioral GREEN and REFACTOR when the required behavior still passes and all active ATDD Bun profiles are green. Only this state is completion.
Phase ordering never suppresses a validator, weakens a threshold, or permits a security, architecture, runtime, traceability or other active constraint to remain violated in review-ready work.
